tfn.s: The village has fewer than twenty permanent residents.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text only says a small number of people live there permanently, not how many.

tfn.s: Civita won the title on its own, without any other town.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "In October 2026, Italy's culture minister announced that Civita and the nearby town of Bolsena had won the title of Italian Capital of Contemporary Art for 2028."

tfn.s: People first built Civita over 2,500 years ago.
tfn.why: The text says: "The village was founded more than 2,500 years ago, but only a small number of people now live permanently in its old centre."

tfn.s: Civita and Bolsena will be given a million euros for cultural work.
tfn.why: The text says: "Their joint project will receive one million euros for cultural activities."

tfn.s: The plans for the arts programme have already produced results.
tfn.why: The text says: "These are plans for the years ahead, not results yet."

focus.note: Many phrasal verbs are a verb plus a small word. The small word, such as down or away, changes the meaning, so choose the one that fits the whole idea.

items.s: The bridge is very high, so some visitors are afraid to look ____ into the valley.

tfn.s: The writer suggests that a busy summer does not prove Civita is a healthy community.
tfn.why: The text contrasts a full bridge in summer with the winter difference between "a successful attraction and a living village".

tfn.s: The text suggests that art can protect the hilltop from further erosion.
tfn.why: The text says: "Art cannot hold the ground together."

tfn.s: Organisers have already chosen the first artists to take part.
tfn.why: The text only says what the organisers hope to develop, not who has been chosen.

tfn.s: Capri, Padua and Pozzuoli all failed to win the 2028 title.
tfn.why: The winning pair is described as "beating other finalists including Capri, Padua and Pozzuoli".

tfn.s: The writer expects the project's real success to be judged before 2028.
tfn.why: The text says: "The true test will come after 2028."

focus.note: Check the form after the gap (-ing, -s or the base form). The small word that follows, such as into, away, back or down, tells you which verb to choose.

tfn.s: The writer implies that Civita looks far busier in summer than it is lived in.
tfn.why: The text contrasts "a crowded visitor route" with "a nearly empty village".

tfn.s: The writer believes cultural projects reliably turn publicity into lasting jobs.
tfn.why: The text says such projects "often struggle to convert short-term attention into durable economic opportunities".

tfn.s: Bolsena will host more of the 2028 events than Civita.
tfn.why: The text does not say how the events will be shared between the two places.

tfn.s: The writer suggests that Civita's problem is shared by other places, though few face it so sharply.
tfn.why: The text says the question "is hardly unique to Civita, but few places in Italy pose it quite so starkly".

tfn.s: The writer says the programme will be judged mainly by the size of the 2028 crowds.
tfn.why: The text says its significance "will depend on what survives it", and that a crowded calendar will not secure a future.

speak.title: Role-play: how to spend the money
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.role: a neighbour who wants practical repairs
a.text: Your small town has won 100,000 euros. You think the money should pay for a safer bridge and a better bus service. Explain why, and ask your neighbour two questions about their idea.

b.role: a neighbour who wants an art festival
b.text: Your small town has won 100,000 euros. You think the money should pay for an art festival that brings visitors and young people. Explain why, and ask your neighbour two questions about their idea.

phrases: I'd rather spend the money on something people can use.
That's a fair point, but it won't last.
What would happen if nobody came?
I'm not sure that's the best idea.
We're not going to agree on everything.
Could we split the money between both plans?
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: how did you decide to spend the money, and was it a fair deal?
